# Introduction {-}

Statistics is the science of collecting, organising, presenting, analysing and interpreting data. It allows us to investigate variation, quantify uncertainty and draw informed conclusions from available information. Statistics therefore plays a vital role in helping us understand the world and make informed decisions. Governments, organisations, businesses, and individuals across a wide range of fields rely on statistics and statisticians.

The *Advanced Higher Statistics* course aims to provide students with a sound foundation in statistical knowledge and methods. This textbook has been designed to provide key facts, examples, and exercises to support students as they progress through the course. It covers the main ideas and methods used in statistical investigations, including:

- Formulating *research questions*.
  
- Collecting data using appropriate *sampling techniques*.

- Exploring data using *descriptive statistics*, such as:
    - Visualising data with charts and graphs.
    - Calculating and interpreting sample statistics.  

- Applying *statistical inference* to evaluate claims about population parameters, including:
    - An introduction to \textit{probability theory}, which underpins statistical inference.  
    - Performing hypothesis tests.  
    - Constructing confidence intervals.  
    
- *Interpreting* results in context and *communicating* findings.

By the end of the course, students should have the knowledge and confidence to collect and analyse their own data, interpret and communicate their findings, and carry out independent statistical investigations.

## Motivation and Structure {-}

This book is primarily a *course textbook*, with a focus on providing clear notes, carefully selected worked examples and thorough exercises for students studying the Advanced Higher Statistics course. 

One motivation for writing this textbook was to minimise the time spent copying detailed notes in class, freeing up more time to explore and investigating ideas to build a better understanding of each concept introduced. For that reason, it does not aim to provide all the interesting practical activities and discussions which are needed to give students the best possible introduction to statistics. Any delivery of the course using this textbook should therefore be supplemented with such activities and discussions.

The book is designed to be worked through in a linear manner, with many chapters building on the knowledge gained from previous chapters. However, with suitable planning, teachers may choose to change the order in which chapters are covered. 

Most sections are designed to correspond to approximately one lesson, although some can be tackled in considerably less time. A typical section contains:

- An introduction to the section's content.

- Key facts to remember, often in bold or set within a note box.

- A worked example demonstrating an appropriate level of detail in its solution.

- A selection of questions designed to test understanding and skills, with increasing levels of challenge.

Each chapter concludes with a review exercise, containing questions written in a style matching that of typical examination questions. These may be useful to set as homework, and suggested marking schemes can be found on the textbook's website.

## Useful Links {-}

The textbook's website, [**advancedhigherstatistics.github.io**](https://advancedhigherstatistics.github.io), contains fully worked solutions to all the exercises, additional proofs, examples, revision material and a selection of practical activities. Should any errors be found in any edition of the textbook, they will be listed there with corrections.

The websites below are all also strongly recommended:

- [Advanced Higher Statistics course information (Qualifications Scotland): www.qualifications.gov.scot](https://www.qualifications.gov.scot).

- [An extensive collection of AH Statistics resources: statistics.nhost.uk](https://statistics.nhost.uk).

- [Dynamic Maths Exam Question Bank: www.dynamicmaths.co.uk](https://www.dynamicmaths.co.uk/QuestionBank/index.php?levelQ=17).

At the time of printing, each link is active and each site is still being maintained. Should that change, updates and any new recommended links can be found on the textbook's website.
